strings.aboutText: A free app with the tools a Muslim needs every day: zakat, inheritance, prayer times, qibla, the Hijri date and a tasbih. Rulings follow the majority of jurists, prayer times use astronomical formulas, and dates follow the Umm al-Qura calendar.

strings.inhDisclaimer: The result is a guide based on the majority view. It does not replace a Sharia court or a scholar of fara'id.

inhNote.MatSiblingsShare: Maternal half-siblings share one third equally, male and female alike.
inhNote.Umariyya: This is one of the two 'Umariyyah cases: the mother takes a third of what remains after the spouse's share.
inhNote.GrandmothersShare: The two grandmothers share one sixth.
inhNote.FullSistersGhayr: Full sisters become residuaries together with the daughters.
inhNote.Akdariyya: This is the Akdariyyah case: the sister is given a half and the grandfather a sixth, raising the case to 9; their shares are then pooled and split two to one, giving 27.
inhNote.JaddRule: With siblings, the grandfather takes whichever is best for him: sharing, or a third of the estate — the majority view (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali). Abu Hanifa held that the grandfather excludes the siblings like the father.
inhNote.JaddRuleOtherFard: With siblings, the grandfather takes whichever is best for him: sharing, or a third of the remainder, or a sixth of the estate — the majority view (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali). Abu Hanifa held that the grandfather excludes the siblings like the father.
inhNote.Muadda: Paternal half-siblings were counted against the grandfather (mu'addah), then their share returns to the full siblings where needed.
inhNote.NothingLeft: Nothing remains after the fixed shares, so the residuary heir ({winner}) receives nothing.
inhNote.Mushtaraka: This is the Mushtarakah (Himariyyah) case: Malikis and Shafi'is let the full siblings share the third with the maternal siblings; the result here follows the Hanafi and Hanbali view.
inhNote.Awl: The fixed shares exceeded the base, so the case was raised from {asl} to {awl} ('awl) and every share shrinks in proportion.
inhNote.Radd: There is no residuary heir, so the surplus is returned to the sharers in proportion to their shares, except the spouses.
inhNote.SpouseOnlyRadd: The only heir is the spouse: many contemporary scholars and several family laws return the remainder to them; earlier scholars gave it to distant kindred, then the public treasury.
inhNote.NoHeirs: There is no sharer or residuary heir; the estate goes to distant kindred, then the public treasury. Refer to the competent court.

onboarding: Muslim tools in one app: prayer, qibla, Quran, zakat and inheritance. No ads, and most of it works offline.
Accurate times for your city with adhan alerts, the qibla by compass, and the Hijri date and Islamic events.
Mushaf pages, tafsir and recitation, focus and memorization modes, and a daily khatma that tracks your progress and streak.
Zakat in its five types, inheritance and expiations — every ruling comes with its evidence from the Quran, the Sunnah and the scholars.
Use the search bar on Home for tools, cities, surahs, ayahs and adhkar, in any language. You can replay this tour from Settings.
strings.privacyText: The app collects no personal data and uses the internet only to download the tafsirs you choose and to play recitations when you ask. Your location is used only on your device to compute prayer times and the qibla, and your settings and numbers stay on your device.
strings.qiblaTip: To change your location, use the Prayer Times page. Hold the phone flat and away from metal for an accurate reading.
strings.quranSources: Quran text (Uthmani script) from the Tanzil Project (tanzil.net). Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex), Tafsir al-Jalalayn and the translations of the meanings from tanzil.net/trans. Quran font: Amiri Quran, SIL Open Font License. Recitations: EveryAyah.com.

evidence.Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to take ch: Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to take charity from people's wealth to purify them; it is the third pillar of Islam.
evidence.The warning against hoarding gold and si: The warning against hoarding gold and silver
evidence.Whoever hoards gold and silver without p: Whoever hoards gold and silver without paying their zakat is warned of punishment, so zakat is due on gold, silver and money.
evidence.Five awaq are 200 dirhams, about 595 g o: Five awaq are 200 dirhams, about 595 g of pure silver.
evidence.Gold nisab, the lunar year and the rate: Gold nisab, the lunar year and the rate
evidence.Twenty dinars are about 85 g of pure gol: Twenty dinars are about 85 g of pure gold. Zakat is due only after a full lunar year, and the rate is one fortieth (2.5%).
evidence.Abu Dawud (1573), graded authentic by al: Abu Dawud (1573), graded authentic by al-Albani
evidence.Scholars agree that the zakat of gold, s: Scholars agree that the zakat of gold, silver and money is one fortieth once it reaches the nisab and a year has passed.
evidence.Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ijma'; Ibn Qudamah, a: Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ijma'; Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni
evidence.The Hanafis require zakat on it, as did: The Hanafis require zakat on it, as did Ibn Baz and Ibn Uthaymin among contemporaries; most Malikis, Shafi'is and Hanbalis exempt permissible jewellery kept for wear. The app lets you choose.
evidence.Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Fatawa Ibn Baz: Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Fatawa Ibn Baz
evidence.Debts you owe that are due now are deduc: Debts you owe that are due now are deducted from your wealth according to the Hanafis and Hanbalis, which the app follows; the later Shafi'i view does not deduct them.
evidence.Zakat on goods held for sale: Zakat on goods held for sale
evidence.Its chain is debated, but the Companions: Its chain is debated, but the Companions such as Umar and Ibn Umar acted on it, and all four schools hold zakat due on trade goods.
evidence.Valued at market price at the end of the: Valued at market price at the end of the year
evidence.Trade goods are added to your money for: Trade goods are added to your money for the nisab, and one fortieth of their value on the day zakat falls due is paid.
evidence.Shares bought for trading are valued at: Shares bought for trading are valued at market price like trade goods; long-term shares owe zakat on their portion of the company's zakatable assets, as decided by the International Islamic Fiqh Academy.
evidence.The letter Abu Bakr wrote for Anas when: The letter Abu Bakr wrote for Anas when sending him to Bahrain, giving the full schedule for camels and sheep; the app calculates by it.
evidence.Nothing is due below thirty; for every t: Nothing is due below thirty; for every thirty a one-year calf, and for every forty a two-year cow.
evidence.They must graze on open pasture most of: They must graze on open pasture most of the year, per the majority, so stall-fed and working animals owe nothing; the Malikis require it on these too. Animals held for sale are valued as trade goods.
evidence.Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Ibn Rushd, Biday: Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Ibn Rushd, Bidayat al-Mujtahid
evidence.The herd must be owned at nisab for a fu: The herd must be owned at nisab for a full lunar year; their young are counted with them.
evidence.Bint makhad: a she-camel of one year; bi: Bint makhad: a she-camel of one year; bint labun: two; hiqqah: three; jadha'ah: four. Tabi' (cattle): one year; musinnah: two. Shah: a sheep of six months or a goat of one year.
evidence.The zakat of crops and fruit is due at h: The zakat of crops and fruit is due at harvest; no year needs to pass.
evidence.A tenth (10%) when watered without cost,: A tenth (10%) when watered without cost, by rain or springs; half a tenth (5%) when watered at cost; three quarters of a tenth (7.5%) when half and half.
evidence.Five awsuq are 300 sa', estimated at abo: Five awsuq are 300 sa', estimated at about 612 kg of wheat; it varies slightly by crop.
evidence.For the majority: grains and fruit that: For the majority: grains and fruit that are measured and stored, such as wheat, barley, rice, dates and raisins; Abu Hanifa required it on all produce of the land.
evidence.Rikaz is treasure buried before Islam; a: Rikaz is treasure buried before Islam; a fifth (20%) is due immediately.
evidence.No nisab or year for rikaz: No nisab or year for rikaz
evidence.The majority take a fifth of any amount: The majority take a fifth of any amount without waiting a year; the Shafi'is require the nisab.
evidence.Hanbalis: one fortieth on any mineral wo: Hanbalis: one fortieth on any mineral worth the gold nisab; Malikis and Shafi'is limit it to gold and silver; Hanafis treat it like rikaz (a fifth). The app uses one fortieth.
evidence.Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; al-Kasani, Bada': Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; al-Kasani, Bada'i' al-Sana'i'
evidence.It is due for every Muslim and those he: It is due for every Muslim and those he supports: one sa' of the local staple food, before the Eid prayer.
evidence.Pay it on the eve of Eid or a day or two: Pay it on the eve of Eid or a day or two before; do not delay it past the Eid prayer.
evidence.Abu Dawud (1609), graded hasan by al-Alb: Abu Dawud (1609), graded hasan by al-Albani
evidence.The majority require food; the Hanafis a: The majority require food; the Hanafis allow its value in money. A sa' is about 2.04 kg of wheat; for rice 2.5–3 kg is taken as a precaution.
evidence.Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Permanent Commit: Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Permanent Committee fatwas
evidence.Feeding a poor person as fidya: Feeding a poor person as fidya
evidence.Ibn Abbas said it is for the elderly man: Ibn Abbas said it is for the elderly man and woman who cannot fast: for each day they feed a poor person.
evidence.One mudd (about 0.75 kg) per poor person: One mudd (about 0.75 kg) per poor person for the Malikis, Shafi'is and Hanbalis; half a sa' for the Hanafis. The app lets you choose.
evidence.Feed ten poor people with the average fo: Feed ten poor people with the average food of your household, or clothe them, or free a slave; whoever cannot, fasts three days.
evidence.Expiation for intercourse during a Ramad: Expiation for intercourse during a Ramadan day
evidence.In order: free a slave; if not possible,: In order: free a slave; if not possible, fast two consecutive months; if unable, feed sixty poor people — and make up the day.
evidence.1) From the estate, pay the funeral cost: 1) From the estate, pay the funeral costs, then debts, then any bequest to a non-heir up to one third. 2) Give those with fixed shares their Quranic portions: a half, a quarter, an eighth, two thirds, a third and a sixth. 3) What remains goes to the agnatic heirs ('asabah), nearest first. 4) Nearer relatives exclude more distant ones. 5) If the shares exceed the estate, all are reduced in proportion ('awl); if something is left and there is no 'asabah, it returns to the sharers other than the spouses (radd).
evidence.The verse of children and parents: The verse of children and parents
evidence.Children: a son receives twice a daughte: Children: a son receives twice a daughter's share. One daughter alone takes a half, two or more take two thirds. Father and mother: each takes a sixth if the deceased has children. If there are no children and the parents inherit, the mother takes a third and the father the rest; if the deceased has siblings (two or more), the mother takes a sixth. All of this is after any bequest and debt.
evidence.The verse of spouses and maternal siblin: The verse of spouses and maternal siblings
evidence.Husband: a half if the wife has no child: Husband: a half if the wife has no children, a quarter if she has. Wife: a quarter if the husband has no children, an eighth if he has; several wives share it. Maternal siblings in kalalah: one takes a sixth, two or more share a third equally, males and females alike.
evidence.The kalalah verse: full and paternal sib: The kalalah verse: full and paternal siblings
evidence.When the deceased leaves no child and no: When the deceased leaves no child and no father: one sister takes a half, two or more take two thirds; if they are brothers and sisters together, a male takes twice a female's share; a brother inherits all of his sister's estate if she has no child.
evidence.The remainder goes to the nearest male a: The remainder goes to the nearest male agnate
evidence.After the fixed shares, the nearest agna: After the fixed shares, the nearest agnate takes the rest: the son, then the son's son, then the father, then the grandfather, then brothers and their sons, then paternal uncles and their sons.
evidence.A son's daughter with a daughter; sister: A son's daughter with a daughter; sisters with daughters
evidence.A son's daughter with one daughter takes: A son's daughter with one daughter takes a sixth to complete two thirds, and full or paternal sisters with daughters become residuaries and take the remainder.
evidence.The Prophet ﷺ gave the grandmother a six: The Prophet ﷺ gave the grandmother a sixth, as al-Mughirah and Muhammad ibn Maslamah testified (Abu Dawud 2894), and there is consensus on it when there is no mother. The paternal grandfather takes the father's place when there is no father; scholars differ on the grandfather with siblings.
evidence.Bequests are limited to a third: Bequests are limited to a third
evidence.A bequest may not exceed a third of the: A bequest may not exceed a third of the estate unless the heirs consent, and there is no bequest to an heir (Abu Dawud 2870, al-Tirmidhi 2120).
evidence.There is no inheritance between people o: There is no inheritance between people of different religions, and neither a deliberate killer nor a slave inherits.
evidence.The school followed in the calculation: The school followed in the calculation
evidence.The app follows the majority on exclusio: The app follows the majority on exclusion, 'awl, radd and the 'Umariyyatan, and notes disputed cases such as the grandfather with siblings and al-Mushtarakah. For large or complex estates, consult a Sharia court or a qualified scholar.
evidence.Allah made the prayers obligatory at kno: Allah made the prayers obligatory at known times; they are not prayed before them nor delayed past them without an excuse.
evidence.From the sun's decline to the night, and: From the sun's decline to the night, and the dawn
evidence.The verse gathers the five times: Dhuhr: The verse gathers the five times: Dhuhr and Asr from the sun's decline, Maghrib and Isha until the dark of night, and the recitation at dawn.
evidence.The times are calculated from it: the su: The times are calculated from it: the sun's zenith for Dhuhr, an object's shadow for Asr, sunset for Maghrib, the disappearance of twilight for Isha, and true dawn for Fajr.
evidence.Asr begins, for the majority, when an ob: Asr begins, for the majority, when an object's shadow equals its length, and for the Hanafis when it is twice its length. Organizations differ on the sun's depression for Fajr and Isha (Muslim World League 18° and 17°, Umm al-Qura 18.5° and Isha 90 minutes after Maghrib), so the app lets you choose the method used in your country.
evidence.Facing the qibla is a condition of the p: Facing the qibla is a condition of the prayer, and the qibla is the Ka'bah in Makkah.
evidence.Facing the direction is enough when far: Facing the direction is enough when far away
evidence.The Prophet ﷺ said it to the people of M: The Prophet ﷺ said it to the people of Madinah, and the majority hold that whoever cannot see the Ka'bah need only face its direction by his best effort; a slight deviation does no harm.
evidence.Al-Tirmidhi (342) and Ibn Majah (1011),: Al-Tirmidhi (342) and Ibn Majah (1011), graded authentic
evidence.How the app finds the direction: How the app finds the direction
evidence.It calculates the shortest path over the: It calculates the shortest path over the earth's surface (the great circle) from your location to the Ka'bah, the approach used by astronomical and religious bodies. Keep the phone away from metal and magnets for an accurate compass.
evidence.Allah made the new moons a measure of ti: Allah made the new moons a measure of time for people's worship and dealings, such as fasting, Hajj and the waiting period.
evidence.Twelve months, four of them sacred: Twelve months, four of them sacred
evidence.The number of months with Allah is twelv: The number of months with Allah is twelve, among them the sacred months: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab.
evidence.The month begins with the sighting: The month begins with the sighting
evidence.Ramadan and the two Eids begin with the: Ramadan and the two Eids begin with the sighting of the crescent, or by completing thirty days.
evidence.The calculated calendar and the sighting: The calculated calendar and the sighting
evidence.The app shows the calculated Umm al-Qura: The app shows the calculated Umm al-Qura calendar, suitable for general dates. For the start of Ramadan and the Eids, follow the announcement of the religious authority in your country, which may differ by a day.
evidence.Resolutions of the Islamic Fiqh Academy: Resolutions of the Islamic Fiqh Academy
evidence.Allah made fasting it obligatory, and in: Allah made fasting it obligatory, and in it the Quran was revealed.
evidence.Better than a thousand months; seek it i: Better than a thousand months; seek it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan, as in Bukhari (2017).
evidence.Fasting the day of Arafah is recommended: Fasting the day of Arafah is recommended for those not on Hajj, and Ashura on the 10th of Muharram, preferably with the 9th.
evidence.Muslims have two Eids: al-Fitr on the 1s: Muslims have two Eids: al-Fitr on the 1st of Shawwal and al-Adha on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.
evidence.Allah commands the believers to remember: Allah commands the believers to remember Him often and glorify Him morning and evening.
evidence.The tasbih counter's presets follow it:: The tasbih counter's presets follow it: 33 tasbih, 33 tahmid, 33 takbir, completing the hundred.
A light remembrance with a great reward.
evidence.Counting on fingers or with a counter: Counting on fingers or with a counter
evidence.Counting on the fingers is better, per t: Counting on the fingers is better, per the hadith «count on your fingertips, for they will be questioned and made to speak» (Abu Dawud 1501, al-Tirmidhi 3583); using beads or a counter is permissible according to most scholars.
evidence.Religious obligations such as prayer and: Religious obligations such as prayer and fasting begin at puberty.
evidence.If the signs of puberty do not appear, t: If the signs of puberty do not appear, the majority set it at fifteen Hijri years, per Ibn Umar's hadith in Bukhari (2664), and Abu Hanifa at eighteen. That is why the app also shows your age in Hijri years.
evidence.Your daily portion is according to your: Your daily portion is according to your ability; consistency is most beloved to Allah, even if little.
evidence.The app's khatma plans follow it: in a m: The app's khatma plans follow it: in a month, and in a week for whoever is able.
evidence.Every letter is a good deed, multiplied: Every letter is a good deed, multiplied tenfold.
